stories.headline: ‘There’s been no failure,’ police chief says of Bridle Path home invasion suspect let go from hospital
stories.summary: Investigators didn’t know a man who showed up to a Toronto hospital last Thursday with a gunshot wound was wanted in a violent home invasion, Chief Myron Demkiw says.

stories.now: CityNews: Toronto Police Chief Myron Demkiw is defending his officers for not arresting a man who showed up at a hospital with a gunshot wound not long after a violent Bridle Path home invasion, saying despite noting a possible…
stories.backstory: The attack drew national attention because it took place in the Bridle Path, one of Toronto's wealthiest neighbourhoods. The family's father, David Morton, CEO of MAC Group, has called the experience terrifying and urged anyone with information to come forward. Police say it was the 119th home invasion reported in Toronto this year, up about 32% from the same period in 2025. Chief Myron Demkiw promised a stronger police presence in the area.

stories.backstory: Reports of tampered Halloween candy surface most years, but confirmed cases are rare and police usually treat each one as a possible criminal act. Tampering with food can lead to charges such as administering a noxious thing or mischief. Police across the GTA routinely advise parents to inspect treats before children eat them. This year's reports come from several places in the same weekend, which is why police are asking anyone with concerns to come forward.
